entity.description: A SIP trunk: a provider (or a PBX) that carries calls to and from the phone network. TLS signaling (transportEnumId VtrTls) with SRTP media (VmeSrtp) is the default; UDP or TCP signaling, or plain RTP, needs a provider profile that allows it (VppPlainLan), never a silent downgrade (D-V4). authJson holds the digest credentials, encrypted: {username, password, authUsername, realm, algorithms}; a realm, when set, is the only one they answer, and algorithms the only digest algorithms (SHA-256 first). inboundAddresses are the provider's signaling addresses (IPs or CIDRs no wider than a /8, or a /32 for IPv6; comma separated) whose INVITEs need no digest. Only a trunk whose profile is a PBX's (VppPlainLan) takes calls signed with its digest credentials from other addresses; a provider's credentials never sign a call in. statusId is what the SIP engine last reported: registered (or reachable without registering), failed with lastErrorText.

A number a trunk brings, in E.164 (+15551234567). A call to it goes where routeTypeEnumId and routeId say: PnrUser rings that user (routeId the userId) under their call handling rules, PnrRingGroup that ring group (routeId its ringGroupId, V3), PnrIvr an IVR menu and PnrQueue a call queue (routeId its ivrMenuId or callQueueId, V5), PnrVoicemail is the voicemail access number. A number's emergency location is the one its calls report. messagingBridgeId is its SMS connector (C4).
A caller-ID grant: the user may present this number on the calls they place, from fromDate until thruDate. Without a grant a user's call goes out with no number of theirs and is refused.

Where a caller is, for emergency calls (§5.2, D-V2): a dispatchable address validated with the trunk provider (providerReference, its id for the address), the callback number emergency services call back, and the notification destination told of each emergency call (notifyEmailAddress; the voice admins are told too). It does not use Mantle's PostalAddress. Only a validated location with a callback number and a notification destination makes emergency calling ready.

A user's phone permissions: outbound calls at all, international and premium destinations (also off until the deployment's VoicePolicy allows them), their registered emergency location, and their own limits (maxConcurrent calls at once, maxPerDay; empty uses the policy's).

field.name: forwardEnabled
field.description: V3: the user's calls may be forwarded to outside numbers (their handling rules and simultaneous ring), within the classes outboundEnabled, internationalEnabled and premiumEnabled allow

entity.description: The deployment's fraud policy (§5.2), one row, voicePolicyId DEFAULT; with no row the defaults apply. International and premium destinations are off until enabled here and for the user. The limits bound the calls at once (all and per user) and per day; failed digest attempts from one source address are blocked after authFailureLimit in authFailureWindowSeconds for authBlockSeconds, and the alertUserGroupId hears of each block. homeCountryCode makes national numbers E.164; emergencyNumbers and premiumPrefixes are comma separated.

Failed SIP digest attempts from one source address, and its block (blockedUntilDate). Blocks are per source and never lock an account: a scanner guessing a user's credentials must not lock that user out. alertedDate is when the admins heard of the current block.

A server whose SIP engine is up: its instance id (the cluster's), the SIP and SIP-over-TLS addresses it listens on, its RTP port range, and the last time it said it was up (every 20 seconds, as a CallMediaNode). A phone call goes to a node that is both a live SipNode and a live CallMediaNode.

A user's voicemail box, made the first time a call to them goes to voicemail or they open its settings (a ring group's box, ringGroupId, V3, is shared by its members: any of them reads it, and a message one of them heard is heard for all). pinHash is the PIN for phone access (argon2, salted; empty: no phone access). greetingLocation is the user's own greeting, under dbresource://moqui/call/voicemail/greeting/ (empty: the default greeting). notifyEmail: an address told of each new voicemail, with a link to it; attachAudio and attachTranscript put the audio and the transcript in that message (off by default: mail cannot be recalled). rings: how many rings (6 seconds each) before a call goes to voicemail (empty: call_ring_seconds). The pin* fields are the box's failed PIN entries over the phone: past the limit the box refuses PINs until pinBlockedUntil, whatever source tries.

field.name: ringGroupId
field.description: A ring group's box (V3): its members share it

entity.description: A message left in a box: the call it came on, the caller's number, when, how long, and the audio (Ogg Opus under dbresource://moqui/call/voicemail/, read only through VoicemailServices get#VoicemailAudio by the box's owner). heardDate is empty until it is played or marked heard (a ring group's box shares it among its members). folder: inbox or trash; trash is emptied after voicemail_trash_days (the audio and its transcripts go too). statusId: VmsStored, or VmsAudioFailed when the audio could not be stored (the message is kept so its owner knows of it). The transcript is a CallTranscript with this voicemailId.

field.name: noticeSentDate
field.description: When the email notice went (sent once)

entity.description: Failed voicemail PIN entries over the phone from one source (the caller's number, which a caller can fake, so the box's own count in VoicemailBox is the real limit), and its block. A box number that has no box is counted here too, under its key, so a refusal never tells whether a box exists.

A user's desk or soft phone that registers with Moqui's registrar: its generated SIP username and the realm its credentials are for, a name, the revision of its credentials (each rotation adds one, which ends the older verifiers and their bindings), its profile (deviceProfile standard: SHA-256 digest only; legacy: MD5 too, for a phone that has no SHA-256), its status (SdsActive, SdsRevoked) and when it last registered. The password is never stored: it is shown once, and only its verifiers are kept (SipDeviceVerifier).

A device's digest verifier for one algorithm and realm: HA1, the hash of username:realm:password (RFC 7616 §3.4.2, RFC 8760), encrypted. A standard device has a SHA-256 one only; a legacy device an MD5 one too. credentialRevision is its device's revision when it was made; a rotation deletes the older ones.

A binding of a registered device (RFC 3261 §10, RFC 5626), as the SIP engine of instanceId holds it: the Contact URI, the flow it came over (transport, the source address and port as rport gives them; a call to the phone goes back over it), its Call-ID and CSeq, its Outbound instance (+sip.instance) and reg-id when it uses Outbound, when it expires and was last refreshed, and the phone's user agent. Expired or revoked bindings cannot ring; the engine removes a row when its binding ends, and expire#SipRegistrations removes those whose engine went away.

Business hours: the weekly hours, dated hours and holidays of its CommsScheduleRule rows, read in its timeZone (an IANA name; empty: the server's). A user's own schedule (ownerUserId) is for their call handling rules; one with no owner is the deployment's, kept by voice admins, for ring groups and for anyone's rules. A calendar-based schedule from a provider (BOSS's calendar) is not built yet.

One rule of a schedule. CsrWeekly: open on dayOfWeek (1 Monday to 7 Sunday) from fromTime until thruTime (HH:mm, local; a thruTime at or before fromTime runs past midnight). CsrDate: open on onDate (yyyy-MM-dd) through thruDate (empty: that day) from fromTime until thruTime (empty: all day), in place of the weekly hours. CsrHoliday: closed on onDate through thruDate, whatever the weekly hours say. repeatYearly: the dates are each year's (month and day). A date covered by a dated rule (a holiday or dated hours) is read from those alone.

A ring or hunt group: a number routed to it (PhoneNumber PnrRingGroup) rings its members by strategy: RgsSimultaneous (all at once, their tabs and phones), RgsInOrder (one at a time by sequenceNum, ringSeconds each) or RgsRoundRobin (in order, starting after the member rung first last time: lastMemberUserId). Members in do not disturb, or in a call with call waiting off, are skipped. With nobody answering, or outside its schedule (commsScheduleId, when set), the fallback runs: RgfVoicemail (the group's own box, which its members share), RgfGroup (another group, fallbackId), RgfNumber (an outside number, fallbackId, through the full fraud policy) or RgfNone (the call ends).
A user in a ring group, rung in sequenceNum order by the in-order and round-robin strategies.
A user's list of callers for their selective rules (forward, reject, accept).
A caller on a list: a number in E.164, or a prefix of one ending in * (+1555*); name is a note.

One of a user's call handling rules (§5.3, Zimbra's call features), read in sequenceNum order for a call to them: ChrAnonymousReject (callers with no number), ChrSelectiveReject, ChrSelectiveAccept (only the callers on its list ring; the others go to the target, voicemail or a refusal), ChrSelectiveForward (the callers on its list go to the target), ChrAlways (every call goes to the target), ChrBusy (when the user is in a call and call waiting is off) and ChrNoAnswer (when nobody answers). The target: ChtNumber (an outside number, targetId; through the fraud policy and the user's forward permission), ChtUser, ChtGroup (targetId), ChtVoicemail or ChtReject. callerListId names the list of a selective rule. With commsScheduleId the rule applies only while the schedule is open (scheduleWhen open, the default) or closed (closed). disabled keeps a rule without it applying.

moqui.basic.Enumeration.description: Accept only callers on a list

entity.description: A user's own phone settings beside their rules (do not disturb is UserStatus's): callWaiting (a call to them while they are in one rings them too; off by default, so it goes to their busy rule or voicemail), their mobile number and ringMobile (it rings at the same time as their tabs and phones, as a call through a trunk under the fraud policy and their forward permission; mobileScheduleId: only while that schedule is open), and hideCallerId (their outbound calls withhold their number: Privacy id, RFC 3323).

The handling plan of an inbound phone call, made when it arrives: its steps (planJson: ring these users and numbers for so long, then the next; a voicemail box; a refusal; the end), the step it is on, and how many forwards it took (hopCount, bounded by call_forward_max_hops). The SIP engine's ring timer and a forward that fails move it on (CallHandlingServices advance, through begin#Voicemail). stepSeq counts the steps run: the engine's timer and the services' voicemail control carry it as stepToken, so one of a step the plan already left does nothing.

An auto attendant menu: a number routed to it (PhoneNumber PnrIvr), an option or a queue's fallback plays its prompt (promptLocation, Ogg Opus the admin uploaded under dbresource://moqui/call/prompt/; without one a tone pattern) and takes the caller's key (maxDigits 1), or up to maxDigits keys ended by # (an extension). No key in timeoutSeconds plays it again, up to maxRetries times, then the timeout target runs; a key no option has runs the invalid target (without one it counts as a retry). Outside its schedule (commsScheduleId) the closed target runs instead. Each target is a CallTarget (CtgUser, CtgGroup, CtgQueue, CtgMenu, CtgVoicemail, CtgNumber, CtgRepeat, CtgEnd) with its id: a userId, ringGroupId, callQueueId, ivrMenuId, voicemailBoxId or outside number.
A key (or keys, for a menu of several digits) of a menu and where it goes; promptLocation, when set, plays before the call goes there ("connecting you to sales").
An inbound call in the IVR: the menu it is in, how many menus it went through (menuCount, bounded so a loop of menus ends) and the keys it chose (pathText, for history and support).

A call queue: a number routed to it (PnrQueue), an IVR option or a transfer puts a call in it; the caller hears hold music (holdMusicLocation, else the deployment's call_hold_music_location, else a tone pattern) and, every announceSeconds, their place in the queue. Its agents (CallQueueAgent) are offered calls in order by strategyEnumId: CqsLongestIdle (the agent idle longest), CqsRoundRobin (after the last one offered, lastAgentUserId) or CqsAllAtOnce, each offer ringing ringSeconds. After a call an agent is in wrap-up for wrapUpSeconds. A call that waited maxWaitSeconds, one that finds maxLength calls waiting, or one outside its schedule goes to the fallback (a CallTarget).

A user who takes a queue's calls: logged in (loggedIn Y) and not paused, not in a call (UserStatus.inCall) and out of wrap-up (wrapUpUntilDate) they are offered its calls. lastCallEndDate (or loggedInDate) is how long they have been idle, for the longest-idle strategy.

A call waiting in a queue, and what became of it: CqeWaiting (with an offer ringing when offeredDate is set, to offerUserIds), CqeAnswered (answeredUserId), CqeAbandoned (the caller hung up), CqeOverflow (it went to the fallback). lastAnnounceDate is when the caller last heard their place.

A transfer of a call's outside party (its phone leg, heldLegId) by fromUserId to a user, an outside number or a queue (targetTypeEnumId CtgUser, CtgNumber, CtgQueue; targetId): CtkBlind (the transferring leg leaves at once, the far end hears ringing until the target answers) or CtkAttended (the far end is on hold while the user consults the target, then completes or cancels). statusId CtsRinging, CtsConsulting, CtsCompleted, CtsCanceled or CtsFailed; one open transfer a call, and a request must name the call's current revision.

Whether the person at otherNumber has opted out of texts from our phoneNumber: STOP (and its synonyms) sets optedOut Y, START sets it N; HELP is kept as the last keyword. A send to an opted-out pair is refused before the provider (reasonCode optedOut).
Texts sent a day, for the limits (VoicePolicy smsMaxPerUserPerDay, smsMaxPerDay): counterKey is user:(userId), system (the sends with no user) or all; dayDate the day in UTC (yyyy-MM-dd).

field.name: smsMaxPerUserPerDay
field.description: Texts a user may send a day (200 when empty)

field.name: smsMaxPerDay
field.description: Texts the deployment sends a day (2000 when empty)

field.name: smsSystemNumber
field.description: The number the system's own texts (a sign-in code) go from; it needs a messaging bridge

field.name: receiptStatus
field.description: What the network's delivery receipt last said: sent, delivered, failed or unconfirmed (C4-SMS)
